chunks: And it is narrated from Khālid ibn Najīḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said:
They discussed misfortune in his presence, so he said:

"Misfortune is in three things: in a woman, a mount, and a house. As for the misfortune of a woman, it is the largeness of her dowry and her disobedience to her husband. As for the mount, it is its bad temperament and its withholding of its back. And as for the house, it is the narrowness of its courtyard, the evil of its neighbors, and the abundance of its defects."

key_terms.الشُّؤْمُ: misfortune or ill-omen described in relation to difficult worldly conditions
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman or wife as one of the three areas mentioned
key_terms.سُوءُ خُلُقِهَا: its bad temperament or ill nature
key_terms.مَهْرِهَا: her dowry, cited here as burdensome when excessive

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, in what things is misfortune found?
ai.summary: This hadith describes forms of misfortune associated with three worldly matters: a woman, a riding animal, and a house. It identifies such misfortune through difficult practical traits such as a high dowry, poor temperament, narrow living space, harmful neighbors, and many defects.
